hed: Houthis take Perim Island in Bab el-Mandeb as Saudi jets strike Mocha airport
dek: Iran-backed Houthi forces reached and occupied Perim Island (Mayun) in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on Friday after Saudi-aligned Yemeni government troops withdrew, officials told the Associated Press, Reuters, and AFP. The barren volcanic island sits in the middle of the narrow waterway linking the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden. Houthis also took the mainland coastal town of Dhubab facing the island a day after seizing the port of Mocha; a Houthi broadcaster said Saudi aircraft struck Mocha’s airport Friday with no immediate casualty report. Brent crude remains on track to end the week above $100 as the advance tightens pressure on a second energy corridor while Hormuz traffic stays constrained.

byline: Event summary from public reporting and named outlets

cl.body: The Associated Press, NBC News, and AFP/France 24 emphasize the government withdrawal from Perim and Dhubab, Saudi airstrikes on Mocha airport, U.N. reports of tens of thousands displaced along the Red Sea coast, and warnings that the offensive risks ending Yemen’s fragile truce and widening the U.S.–Iran war onto a second shipping corridor.

cr.body: Reuters (via CNA), Fox News, and OilPrice.com frame the Perim/Dhubab push as Iran-aligned leverage over Bab el-Mandeb energy and Suez-bound trade after Hormuz disruption, noting Saudi reliance on the Red Sea bypass, oil near multi-month highs, and Riyadh’s request for U.S. strikes that Axios reported Trump declined.

stack_blurb: Perim Island falls; Saudi jets hit Mocha; Bab el-Mandeb risk rises.
seo_description: Houthi forces occupied Perim Island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on Sept. 11 after government withdrawal; Saudi aircraft struck Mocha airport as oil stays above $100.
